incidents.name: Incident with Git Operations and Pull Requests

incident_updates.body:
On November 10, 2026, from approximately 15:00 UTC to 17:55 UTC, GitHub experienced degraded performance affecting repository pages, pull requests, and GitHub Actions. Customers may have seen slow or failed page loads and delays processing pull request updates and merges. Some pull requests continued to display an earlier source-branch commit after the broader service degradation ended. GitHub Actions workflows were delayed for approximately 1.8% of events, peaking at about 7% between 16:30 and 16:50 UTC. Delays were typically 1.5 to 3.5 minutes, up to 10 minutes. Approximately 0.09% of pull request events did not start their workflows and needed to be re-triggered.

The degradation resulted from overload in the shared infrastructure that supports Git operations. Recent changes increased background processing and the work required to compute pull request merges, adding pressure to the same systems used by customer-facing requests. We mitigated the incident by disabling a recent merge-processing optimization, pausing background analysis, and temporarily limiting lower-priority traffic. The temporary limits also restricted access to commit pages for users who were not signed in. Background processing continued to catch up after service health recovered.

We have reduced repeated repository-analysis work and are adding workload-level concurrency controls to better protect customer-facing requests. We are also improving our procedures for safely reducing background load and making pull request synchronization more resilient to temporary failures.

We continue to investigate elevated response times for Git operations and pull requests. Actions workflows are recovering. Pull request processing has shown some improvement, but users continue to experience delays and failures. We’re monitoring the impact and working to restore normal service.
